summary: Osamu Hayashima is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Gadjin Nagao and Noritoshi Aramaki, and at the University of Hamburg (1992). He held posts at Nagasaki University (~1978–1997), Shiga University of Medical Science (~1997–2003), and Ryukoku University (~2003–2012).

Osamu Takata worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, having studied under Baiei Henmi. From around 1965 to 1972, he served as head of the fine arts division at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.
Oscar Botto was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin until around 1943. He also founded the journal Indologica Taurinensia.

Oskar von Hinüber, an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied under Paul Thieme and at Mainz (-1973). He held posts at Mainz (~1974–1981), Nepal Research Centre (1977), Freiburg (1992–1994), Soka University (2004–2007), and IRIAB (2004–2013).
Osmund Bopearachchi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Paul Bernard. Around 1989, he held a post at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique.

Osvald Sirén worked in sinology, history, and archaeology after studying at the University of Helsinki (~1897–1900). He held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923) and the Nationalmuseum (1928–1945).

Othmar Frank, a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and philosophy, studied at Paris (~1814) and London (~1815). He held professorships at Bamberg (~1807), Würzburg (~1821–1826), and Munich (1826).
Otoya Tanaka was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo until around 1927 under Naoshiro Tsuji. He later held a post at Chuo University.

Otto Blau was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1848 to 1852, studying under August Friedrich Pott between roughly 1848 and 1851.
Otto Fischer worked in sinology, japanology, and history and archaeology. He held posts at Kunstmuseum Basel (1927) and the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Otto Franke was a scholar of sinology and Indology who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1882–1883) and the University of Göttingen (~1883–1886). He held posts at the University of Hamburg (~1910–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1931).

Otto Höfler worked in linguistics and history and archaeology, studying at the University of Vienna (~1921–1926) and Lund University (~1928–1935). He held posts at the University of Kiel (~1935–1938), Munich (~1938–1945), and Vienna (~1957–1971).

Otto Neugebauer worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Graz (1919–1921) and Göttingen (1922–1926). He held posts at Göttingen (1926–1934), Copenhagen (1934–1938), Brown (1939–1969), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1969–1990).

Otto Rosenberg specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology. He studied at St. Petersburg University (~1906–1911) under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Sergey Oldenburg, and held a professorship at Saint Petersburg State University from around 1917 to 1919.
Otto Schrader was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1902–1909) and the University of Kiel (~1909–1919).
Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at the philosophy faculty of the German University of Prague under Moriz Winternitz from around 1914 to 1919.
Otto Strauss was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Paul Deussen (~1907–1911). He held a professorship at the University of Kiel from around 1911 to 1920.

Otto von Böhtlingk, an Indologist and linguist, studied at St. Petersburg, Berlin under Franz Bopp, and Bonn under Christian Lassen. He became a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1842 and held a post at Jena (~1868–1885).

P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ceylon, Canterbury, and Hawaii under Eliot Deutsch, and served as a professor at the University of Ceylon from around 1968 to 2006.
P. K. Mukhopadhyay is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and served as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research.
